hills.painterNote: Attempt 2: replace rectangular scan-row fills with irregular angled canopy dabs and wavy mottled grass strokes, merge left-centre oaks into one contiguous forest, deepen/saturate darks and bright grass, and soften trails — because attempt 1 read as flat green boxes/bands instead of loose foliage and sunlit hills.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The build reads as a digital slab-fill reveal — a flat faded sheet, then flat polygonal tree masses with scalloped hard edges and texture dumping in late — rather than a brush-and-pen accumulation of strokes.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence depicts a digital mask reveal or flat color fill rather than a brush-based painting process, characterized by sharp, geometric edges and flat slabs of color.

south-france.painterNote: Attempt 2: shrink and lighten the village into a central column with pale stone walls, thin terracotta roofs and tree gaps between buildings, pale the straw fields, layer varied olive tree masses, and build a distinct bright foreground pine with visible trunk/branches — because a1's houses were an oversized dark-brown block at far right, fields were orange, and trees/pine merged flat.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The build reads as a digital fill rather than brush-and-pen work: a whole-sheet faint wash with subjectless horizontal streaks, then uniform stamp-like foliage dabs and scalloped color blobs, with buildings arriving as flat windowed slabs and no pen-drawing stage at any point.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The shapes are blocky slabs and pixelated rather than organic brushstrokes or pen lines.

sargent.painterNote: Hull as one wet-in-wet tapered silhouette with fan strokes converging to the bow and darker edge glazes, instead of stacked horizontal bands that read as rectangles; also deepen/variegate water and draw chains as continuous rust lines with dabs.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The build-up reads like a genuine watercolor sequence—broad sky and side washes first, then the hull form with reserved white highlights, then dark accents and fine rigging lines last—though the speckled sky texture, flat slab shapes, and the hull arriving as a finished region are noticeable tells.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence mimics a digital opacity reveal rather than a brushstroke progression, with the entire composition visible as a faint ghost before details appear.

mittens.painterNote: Changing cat to a tilted up-looking head with bigger eyes, broken fur texture and mostly-white chest, and man to lower/smaller irregular curly hair with features moved up and softer modelling, because a1 was too symmetric, blocky and separated.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The marks read as a coarse digital fill, not brushwork: stair-stepped slab edges, dash-row stripes, a flat hair mass carried through every stage, and a late dump of fine whisker/face detail that ends on a face unlike the target.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence is logically ordered but the fur is rendered as a grid of squares rather than brush strokes.

trumbull.painterNote: Changing the solid blue roof pyramids into a stone front gable with thin slate roof bands behind it, adding the left tower and right chimneys, darkening and enlarging windows and ground-floor arched doors, softening stone banding into finer texture, and densifying foliage/signpost — because attempt 1 misread the roof/gable geometry and was too pale, flat and regular versus the target.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The building emerges as flat even-toned slabs with scalloped and dotted edges that later receive uniform window blobs and dumped texture, a fill-then-detail sequence rather than a painter's natural drawing-to-wash order.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence begins with a mask-like reveal (faded in) rather than brushwork, and the architectural forms are filled with flat, evenly-toned slabs instead of being built up with strokes.
